title: The Notes
text: "I don’t know," I said, looking at the notes spread across the table. "I know how this looks, and I can’t explain it. But I swear I had nothing to do with this."

title: The Funeral
text: The first thing I noticed about the funeral was that nobody was crying. The second was that the coffin was empty.

title: Bellweather
text: Ask anyone in Bellweather what happened to the Henderson family and they’ll tell you the same story. Word for word.

title: Before You Say Anything
text: "Before you say anything," she whispered, "you need to understand that I wasn’t supposed to survive."

title: Which Version
text: By the time the police arrived, I had already cleaned the kitchen, changed my clothes and decided which version of the truth I would tell.

title: Darla
text: Darla had been to this town a thousand times. She always said she hated it, but that didn’t mean she didn’t understand it. What she couldn’t explain was why the building on Main and Willow had disappeared overnight.

title: Arthur Bellamy
text: Arthur Bellamy delivered the post for forty-three years. He knew everyone’s secrets and had never opened a single letter. Until Tuesday.

title: Evelyn Price
text: Nobody trusted Evelyn Price. She was nosy, opinionated and forever appearing where she wasn’t wanted. Unfortunately, she was also the only person who knew what happened that summer.

title: Detective Vale
text: Detective Marcus Vale was famous for solving impossible cases. His colleagues called it intuition. His wife called it obsession. Marcus knew it was neither.

title: Beatrice
text: Beatrice collected other people’s discarded receipts, photographs and shopping lists. Her family called it hoarding. After thirty years, she finally had enough evidence.

title: Not What Happened
text: "That’s not what happened." Everyone turned to Eleanor. "You weren’t even there," her brother said. Eleanor stared at her wine. "That’s what you think."

title: Guestbook
text: "How many times have you been here?" "Once." "Then why is your name in the guestbook seventeen times?"

title: The Auction
text: The auctioneer raised the photograph. "Do I hear fifty pounds?" "Don’t," someone whispered behind me. "Whatever you do, don’t let anyone buy that photograph."

title: Breakfast
text: "You said your husband left on Monday." "He did." "Then perhaps you can explain why he ordered breakfast here on Wednesday."

title: The Only One
text: "I’m not accusing you of anything," the detective said. "Then why am I here?" "Because you’re the only person who hasn’t asked what happened."

title: Marshfield
text: Marshfield was famous for its flower show, its excellent bakery and the fact that nobody had been born there in twenty-six years.

title: The Mariner’s Rest
text: At the end of the coastal road stood the Mariner’s Rest. Every room was named after a shipwreck. Every room except number seven.

title: December
text: The house had been empty since 1987, its roof collapsing and windows boarded. Yet every December somebody decorated its front door for Christmas.

title: The Invitation
text: Seven people receive invitations to a weekend retreat. Each contains a different photograph. All seven photographs were taken at the same event.

title: Second Property
text: While settling her mother’s estate, Nora discovers thirty years of rent payments for a property nobody in the family has heard of.

title: Wrong Question
text: "You keep asking who took it," Clara said. "You should be asking who put it back."

title: The Gardener
text: Otis tended the cemetery gardens every morning, including one patch of ground with no grave. On Thursday, somebody left flowers there.

title: The Invitation List
text: "That’s impossible," I said. "I wrote the guest list myself." "Then why are there eight place cards?"

title: The Clockmaker
text: Mabel fixed watches for a living and distrusted anyone who said time healed things. Then twelve strangers arrived carrying watches stopped at 9:14.

title: The Clown Doctor
text: Lulu was raised by circus clowns and is now in her third year of medical school. She has a magnificent collection of brightly coloured socks and an unfortunate habit of honking her nose when nervous. Yesterday, a letter arrived from the circus. It contained only a photograph of an empty chair.

title: Before the Wedding
text: Sally received a letter three days before her wedding: “There is something you need to know. Meet me at the café tomorrow at two. I’ll know it’s you.” There was no signature. The handwriting was unmistakably her own.

title: The Last Customer
text: At exactly 4:57 every afternoon, the same woman ordered a cup of tea she never drank.

title: The Borrowed Dog
text: You agree to look after a stranger’s dog for an hour. At the park, six people greet it by six different names. One of them bursts into tears.

title: An Unusual Inheritance
text: Your aunt has left you her entire collection of umbrellas, with one condition: you must never open the yellow one indoors.

title: The Museum Guard
text: Arthur guards a museum room that nobody visits. He is certain one of the portraits changes expression whenever he takes his lunch break.

title: Wrong Number
text: “You’re late,” said the stranger on the phone. “The penguins have already voted.”

title: The Secret Recipe
text: The village baking contest has been won by the same person for 43 years. This year, her recipe book is stolen, and every suspect smells of cinnamon.

title: The Other House
text: The house across the street was exactly like mine, except that every Thursday its windows showed the sea.

title: An Apology in Advance
text: A note slipped beneath your door reads: “I’m sorry for what I’m going to do on Friday. Please remember I meant well.” Today is Tuesday.

title: The Hat Collector
text: Mina owns 117 hats and has never worn the same one twice. The only person who has ever seen her without a hat refuses to discuss it.

title: The Midnight Choir
text: Every night at midnight, the residents of a quiet apartment building hear a choir singing from the locked basement.

title: An Awkward Reunion
text: “You look exactly the same,” she said. “Which is impossible, considering I buried you in 1986.”

title: The Lost & Found
text: A small railway station has a lost-and-found office filled with things nobody remembers losing: a birthday, a sense of direction, a first kiss.

title: The Accidental Mayor
text: Nico thought he was entering a raffle for a fruit basket. He woke up the next morning as mayor of a town he had never visited.

title: The Good Luck Spoon
text: A battered silver spoon has passed through five generations. Everyone who owns it experiences one extraordinarily lucky Tuesday.

title: Dinner for Seven
text: You set the table for six. When the guests arrive, there are seven place settings and nobody admits to adding the extra chair.

title: The Applause
text: The first time I heard applause coming from my wardrobe, I assumed it was the neighbours.

title: The Ferry
text: A ferry crosses a narrow bay once a day. On the final crossing of the season, the captain announces that the boat will not be returning.

title: The Unfinished Portrait
text: Esme paints portraits of people she has never met. Yesterday, a man knocked on her door carrying the exact coat she had painted that morning.

title: The Wrong Suitcase
text: At the airport, you discover your suitcase contains 26 identical postcards, a single tap shoe and a handwritten map of your hometown.

title: A Tiny Kingdom
text: Inside an antique dollhouse, someone has placed a newspaper reporting an event that hasn’t happened yet.

title: The Lighthouse Keeper
text: Pip has lived beside the lighthouse all her life, despite being terribly afraid of the sea. Tonight, the light is shining inland.

title: The Wedding Cake
text: The wedding cake arrives with the correct names, correct date and a miniature bride and groom who look nothing like the couple.

title: The Extraordinary Ordinary
text: There was nothing remarkable about Wednesday until the pigeons started returning my mail.

title: The Neighbour’s Garden
text: A narrow garden between two houses blooms with flowers nobody can identify. Each morning, a new path appears.

title: The Spare Key
text: You find a key in your coat pocket with a tag that reads: “For the door you haven’t noticed yet.”

title: The Audition
text: “Can you cry on command?” asked the director. “No,” I said, “but I can make everyone else cry.”

title: The Last Dance
text: Beatrice, 82, teaches ballroom dancing in the village hall. She has kept one dance card untouched since she was nineteen.

title: The Uninvited Guest
text: Everyone at the dinner party remembers inviting the same guest. Nobody can agree on who they are.

title: The Bookshop Receipt
text: A secondhand book contains a receipt dated tomorrow and a note: “Do not let her finish chapter twelve.”

title: The Rainmaker
text: Felix claims he can predict rain by listening to old radios. He has been wrong every day for a year—until this morning.

title: The Silent Parade
text: Once a year, a parade passes through town without music, banners or spectators. This year, it stops outside your house.

title: The Confession Booth
text: At a village fête, a homemade confession booth promises to reveal your greatest secret for fifty cents. You decide to try it.

title: The Impossible Postcard
text: A postcard arrives from a place you invented in a childhood story. The message says: “Please come back. We need you.”

title: The Borrowed Name
text: Ada changes her name every time she moves to a new town. She has just arrived somewhere everyone already knows her.

title: The Orchard
text: At the edge of the village stands an orchard where every tree bears a different kind of fruit—and one bears tiny brass bells.

title: The Unusual Interview
text: “Tell me about your previous experience,” the interviewer said, carefully closing the trapdoor beneath her desk.

title: The House Rules
text: Your new landlord leaves a list of house rules. Number seven reads: “If the piano starts playing, do not join in.”

title: A Very Small Crime
text: Someone has been stealing the dots from every lowercase i in the town newspaper. The editor offers a reward.

title: The Birthday Visitor
text: Theo celebrates his birthday on a different day each year. This year, a stranger arrives claiming they share the same birthday—and the same memories.

title: The Mapmaker
text: Iris draws maps of places that no longer exist. One afternoon, a child asks her for directions to a place that has never existed.

title: The Elevator
text: On the ninth floor, the lift stopped and announced, in my grandmother’s voice, “You really should have called.”

title: The Picnic Basket
text: An old picnic basket always contains exactly what you need, but never what you asked for.

title: The Sleeping Village
text: You arrive at a village where everyone sleeps from noon until sunset. Nobody will explain what happens while they are awake.

title: The Replacement
text: A new employee arrives at your workplace with your name, your handwriting and a surprisingly convincing story about being you.

title: The Little Theatre
text: A travelling puppet theatre appears in the square overnight. The puppets are performing scenes from yesterday.

title: The Letter Writer
text: Ruth makes a living writing difficult letters for strangers. One day she is asked to write a goodbye letter to herself.

title: The Unfinished Song
text: You find a music box that plays the first half of a melody. Every person who hears it claims to know a different ending.

title: The Detour
text: We took the wrong road on purpose, which is how we came to the town that was holding a funeral for its own clock.
